messages.content: I checked with Arun and Thursday is definitely out. Rates are moving, so I want to decide tonight. The two realistic packages are still Friday Dec 11 to Sunday Dec 13 for the three of us: LGA midday flights with the Midtown breakfast hotel, or Newark with the Upper West Side boutique. Which would you book?

I would book the LGA flight pair plus the Midtown breakfast-included hotel, assuming the room really has the bed setup you need. For a two-night December weekend with a child, the airport and timing are doing a lot of work: LGA keeps Friday from turning into a late arrival, and the late-afternoon Sunday return gives you a real morning without pushing bedtime too badly. The Midtown room is the weak spot because it is compact, but breakfast included and a shorter transfer reduce friction.
The gap is about $420 more than the Newark plus boutique package. LGA plus the Upper West hotel is another $160 above the Midtown plan.

That makes the tradeoff pretty clear: cheapest is Newark plus Upper West, but it buys savings with a later, less predictable arrival; nicest neighborhood is LGA plus Upper West, but it costs the most and still leaves breakfast out; best balance is LGA plus Midtown, because it spends the premium on the part that matters most on a short family weekend: getting in smoothly and getting moving Saturday morning.
Are the small rooms going to make us regret it?

Only if the bed setup is not guaranteed or you expect to spend much time in the room. For two nights, I would tolerate compact if it has two real beds or a confirmed bed plus sleeper arrangement, a solid guest rating, and luggage storage. If it is one queen with a rollaway request, I would not book it.
It says two double beds, not queens. Breakfast is included. Rating is 4.3. Cancellation until Dec 8.

Two doubles is less comfortable than two queens, but for one child and two nights it is workable. The 4.3 rating, included breakfast, and Dec 8 cancellation window keep it safe. I would just verify whether the room category is guaranteed after booking, not merely requested.
What if Newark is fine and we save the money for shows and meals?

It is a reasonable backup. I would choose Newark only if the $420 is a firm budget issue or if the LGA fare jumps before you pay. With holiday traffic, winter weather, and a Friday arrival, Newark adds more transfer risk. You also lose the included breakfast if the boutique is the paired hotel, so some of the savings will get eaten each morning.
Sunday flight is around 4:45 back to Atlanta. Is that too late?

No, that is the right window. It avoids a rushed checkout-only morning, but you should still be home before it feels like a red-eye. I would avoid anything much after 6 unless it is dramatically cheaper.
Okay, I think we book the LGA and Midtown option. Anything I should check before I click purchase?

Yes: confirm the fare is nonstop both ways, all three travelers are on the same reservation, baggage and seat-selection rules are acceptable, the hotel total includes taxes and any facility fee, the two-double room is guaranteed, breakfast hours work for Saturday and Sunday, and cancellation is truly free until Dec 8. After purchase, pick seats together; if there is a window within the three-seat grouping, take it, but do not split everyone up just for that.
Done. Flights and hotel are booked. I grabbed the cancellation email and the fare receipt.

Good choice. Save the hotel confirmation with the room type, cancellation deadline, breakfast language, and any fee disclosure. Also save the flight receipt, confirmation codes, and seat map screenshots. Next follow-up items: call or message the hotel to confirm the two-double setup and luggage storage, check seats again after ticketing, and plan airport transfers once the weather forecast is clearer.

messages.content: We leave for New York next Friday. Can you give me the no-drama checklist? Flights and the Midtown hotel are booked now.

Checklist: check in exactly when it opens; keep everyone on the same reservation and seated together; screenshot boarding passes, hotel confirmation, breakfast hours, and cancellation/fee details; pack rain layers and comfortable shoes; call the hotel to reconfirm two-double room plus luggage storage; and plan extra margin because holiday crowds and wet weather can slow rideshares.
Hotel confirmed breakfast 6:30 to 10 and luggage storage. They still said bed type is confirmed but subject to room condition, whatever that means.

That usually means the category is confirmed but the exact room is assigned day-of. I would message again 24 hours before arrival: arriving with a child, please hold the confirmed two-double room. Bring a backup mindset, but it is not enough of a warning to change hotels now.
Seats are 18A, 18B, 18C outbound. Coming back they put us in 22B, 22C, 22D. Should I keep checking?

Outbound is ideal: together with a window. For the return, keep the row together. If 22A or another full three-seat set with a window opens, switch; otherwise do not trade the together seating just to get a window.
Do we prebook a ride from LGA, or just grab one when we land?

For arrival, I would not overpay for a black-car hold unless you have lots of luggage. Use taxi or rideshare after landing, then switch to a prebooked ride only if the forecast worsens or your arrival moves later.
What about Sunday back to LGA? Flight is 4:45.

Leave the hotel around 1:45, no later than 2:00 with rain or street closures. Ask the front desk that morning about parade or holiday traffic, and request the ride before you bring bags down. Final day-before items: check in, scan seat map for a better three-seat set, charge devices, download maps, and put breakfast plus indoor backup plans at the top of Saturday morning.

messages.content: New York is behind us. I need to start a Phoenix work trip plan for Jan 25 to Jan 28, but the client has not nailed down the site.

Okay. Before booking, I would build it as a conditional plan. What is known so far: solo or team, first required in-person time, Thursday end time, and whether the site is the central hospital campus or the Scottsdale outpatient location?

Solo for now. Workflow rehearsal is Tuesday and Wednesday, closeout Thursday. Monday may be remote unless they add a late-afternoon kickoff. The site is either the central hospital campus or Scottsdale.

Then I would not buy a nonrefundable hotel yet. Flight shape: use ATL-PHX nonstop if the price is not wild; the cheaper one-stop choices are likely to make the travel day too long. If Monday stays remote, leave Atlanta late morning or early afternoon Monday. If an in-person kickoff is added before about 4 local time, consider Sunday evening instead.
Can you frame two options for approval? Include Delta if it works, but not if the timing is bad.

Option A, central campus: Monday ATL-PHX nonstop leaving late morning, arrive early afternoon; rideshare to a central corridor or downtown hotel; Thursday PHX-ATL nonstop around 5 to 6 after closeout. Option B, Scottsdale: same flight windows, hotel in Old Town or near the outpatient site; consider a rental only if they expect you to move between sites. I would list one-stop flights only as a savings alternative, not the recommended path.
Closeout should end at 2:30 Thursday. I do not want a 6 a.m. Monday flight if Monday might just be calls from the hotel.

Agreed. A 10:30 to noon-ish Atlanta departure is the safer target. Because Phoenix is two hours behind Atlanta in January, that still gets you there early afternoon. It gives room for a 4:30 or 5 p.m. kickoff, but it does not force an unnecessarily early start if Monday is remote.
And Thursday?

Aim for a PHX departure around 5:15 to 6:15 p.m. That leaves time after a 2:30 closeout for final questions, bags, and the airport. I would avoid a 3:30 flight as too tight and avoid anything much later than 7 unless it is the only nonstop or saves a lot.
For hotels I do not need fancy. I do need easy breakfast or coffee before 7:30 and some reasonable dinner option without a long ride.

For the central campus, look at well-rated limited-service hotels around downtown, Midtown, or the Central Avenue corridor with included breakfast or a dependable cafe in the lobby. For Scottsdale, Old Town is better for dinner access, while a hotel directly by the outpatient site is better if mornings are early. In both cases, keep the rating floor at solid guest reviews and book refundable until the site is confirmed.
Do I need a rental car?

Not for a fixed central hospital schedule; rideshare should be enough. For Scottsdale, it depends: one outpatient site plus hotel nearby can still be rideshare, but multiple sites, early starts, or equipment runs would point to a rental. Ask the client before putting that in the approval request.
What exact questions should I send the client?

Ask: 1) first required in-person time on Monday, if any; 2) confirmed address for Tuesday through Thursday; 3) whether Thursday closeout really ends by 2:30; 4) whether any sessions move between the central campus and Scottsdale; 5) visitor parking or badge instructions; and 6) whether they prefer you near the hospital, near Scottsdale, or wherever rates are best.
Can you turn that into a short approval note I can paste to my manager?

Draft: I am planning Phoenix travel for Jan 25 to Jan 28, pending the client confirming the exact site and Monday start time. Recommended travel is ATL-PHX nonstop late morning Monday, returning PHX-ATL nonstop early evening Thursday after the 2:30 closeout. I am avoiding cheaper one-stop options unless savings are substantial because they add too much travel time. Hotel will be refundable and selected near the confirmed site, with reliable guest reviews, breakfast or early coffee, and nearby dinner options. Open items before purchase: client site address, Monday in-person requirement, Thursday end time, and whether rideshare is sufficient or a rental car is needed.
